narr: Showers and thunderstorms developed across northwest North Carolina to the south of a stationary front draped across northern Virginia into central West Virginia. By early afternoon, a surface trough had developed along the lee side of the Blue Ridge Mountains, providing the lower atmospheric convergence needed to aid in thunderstorm development. A couple of the storms increased to severe levels and produced damaging winds which downed trees, while flash flooding occurred with one slow-moving storm that produced an estimated 4 to 5 inches of rainfall within a 2-hour period.
ev: About 6 inches of water was observed flooding over Allen Road near the intersection with Topia Road, most likely caused by Prathers Creek rising out of its banks due to 3 to 5 inches of rain falling within a 2 hour period at rates of up to 5 inches per hour. No damage was reported to the road, and it was reopened to traffic after the flooding receded.
lsr: Several inches of water over the road near the intersection of Topia Road and Allen Road. This flooding was likely caused by water coming out of the banks of Prathers Creek.
